title: Manchester City’s Rodri avoids ban over referee comments, fined £80k
content:
Manchester City midfielder Rodri has been fined £80,000 ($106.9k) but avoided a ban after making “improper” comments about Premier League match officials.

The 29-year-old questioned “not fair” refereeing decisions after City drew  with Tottenham Hotspur in February after leading 2-0 at half time.

The Football Association charged the midfielder with misconduct later that month, leaving Rodri potentially facing a ban, but confirmed today that he would be fined instead.

The fine was reduced by a third, the FA confirmed in written reasons released on Monday, due to the Spain international admitting the charge, issuing a swift apology and English not being his first language.

The controversy arose after Dominic Solanke was judged to have made a fair challenge on City defender Marc Guehi while scoring Tottenham’s first goal.

“I know we won too much and the people don’t want us to win but the referee has to be neutral and for me honestly, it’s not fair,” Rodri had said after the game.

“It’s not fair because we work so hard in these situations and now to make these decisions, we have to move on.

“Of course you need to come back but at the end, when everything is finished, we are frustrated because it’s so clear the foul. He kicked the leg and of course with the push of the action on the ball, the ball goes in.

“We have to pay attention to these little things otherwise it’s going to be difficult for everyone because this league is like this — it’s about small details and everything counts, so I think today is a very tough day for us in this sense.”

The FA ruled that these comments “imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official and/or match officials, contrary to FA Rule E3.1”.

“It doesn’t feel fair when the ultimate result of a match is influenced by an incorrect decision rather than just the performance of the team,” Rodri had explained in response.

The 2024 Ballon d’Or winner also cited “the bad foul by Diogo Dalot on Doku in our match at Manchester United which should have been a red card, and Semenyo’s disallowed goal at Newcastle in the Carabao Cup” as recent refereeing “mistakes”.

Having avoided a ban, Rodri will be available for City’s league fixture against West Ham on Saturday after they have faced Real Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League last 16 tie.
